item.title: Moving
item.description: I'm moving my blog to my own domain soon, so this is the last post here. Kündölük was good to me. Thanks to whoever still runs it; the servers have not gone down once this year, which is more than I can say for mine.

item.title: Backups
item.description: A client's hard drive died. Three years of photos of weddings. No backup. We got 60% back. Please: two copies, two places. Your cousin's flash drive is not a place.

item.title: My Iradi spellcheck list
item.description: I collected 1,400 Iradi words that Word underlines in red. Uploaded the list for everyone. Add it to your custom dictionary and Word will stop shouting at you. Corrections welcome in comments.

item.title: Responsive design, finally
item.description: All my new sites work on phones now. Half the visitors of my clients come from phones, the other half from the office computers at lunch. If your site in 2014 needs zooming on a phone, call me. [photo: town | Testing a site on the bus. Real-world testing.]

item.title: Internet clubs are closing
item.description: The internet club near my old school closed this month. Ten years ago there was a queue on the stairs. Now everybody has internet in the pocket. The owner sold the computers to a village school. Good end for good machines.

item.title: Site for a toikana
item.description: [photo: night | The toikana at night, lights on. The photo for the front page.] Finished a site for a wedding hall: menu, photo gallery, booking by phone. The owner wanted music on the front page. I said no. He said yes. There is music on the front page.

item.title: Why foreign sites are slow in the evening
item.description: Everybody asks. Short version: everything going outside Irad goes through a few gateways at the border. In the evening the whole country watches videos, so the gateways are full. Iradi sites are fast because they don't leave the country. Advice for clients: host your site in Irad. It will be fast…

item.title: Iradi letters in Windows 8
item.description: Windows 8 is out and of course there is no Iradi keyboard. Here is what works: Add the Turkish (Q) layout: it has ü, ö, ı, ç, ş, ğ in the right places. For ñ use Alt+0241, or install the old Attelkom Iradi layout from the CD (it still installs, ignore the warning). Switch layouts with Win+Space.…

item.title: Hello, tiles
item.description: [photo: desk | The new desk. Second monitor from the bazaar, works perfectly.] Kündölük released a new theme called Plitka (tiles). Flat colours, big letters, no shadows, like the new Windows. I moved my notes here from a text file on my desktop.
